title: NotNotes Java presentation fixture and web-quality visual doctrine
summary: The NotNotes Java surface remains a renderer/conformance fixture used to drive Swing toward web-client visual quality while preserving the semantic authority boundary. Dev13 extends generic detail-card hierarchy: projected definition labels become section headings, projected status receives compact renderer-owned chip presentation, and empty projected read-only values show an explicit muted placeholder.
invariants: NotNotes domain vocabulary must not become a required generic Wire Swing protocol dependency.
Stable document identity is projected semantic identity, never JList index or native component identity.
Projected label/status/type/owner/meta/subtitle may affect pixels only; extra display metadata must not be returned as semantic authority.
Navigation highlighting is local renderer state and does not itself navigate or grant action authority.
The web client is a visual-quality benchmark, not a source of browser-owned business truth.
Actual desktop capture is required for meaningful presentation changes; semantic traces remain the cross-renderer authority test.
A SEMANTIC_RECORD definition label may become a renderer-owned section heading without creating a business/document concept in Swing.
Projected record status may be compacted visually while the full status remains available to tooltip/accessibility; it must not decide lifecycle feasibility.
An explicit empty-value placeholder is renderer presentation and is never written back to application state.
